propertiesClass.name: clientForm
propertiesClass.defaultValue:
this.fb.nonNullable.group({
    nombre: ['', [
      Validators.required, 
      Validators.minLength(3),
      Validators.maxLength(40),
      Validators.pattern(/^[a-zA-ZáéíóúÁÉÍÓÚñÑ\s]+$/),
      maxWordsValidator(2)
    ]],
    telefono: ['', [
      Validators.required,
      Validators.minLength(8),
      Validators.maxLength(15),
      Validators.pattern(/^\+?[\d\s\-]+$/)
    ]]
  })

components.templateData:
<ion-modal [isOpen]="isOpen()" (didDismiss)="didDismiss.emit()">
  <ng-template>
    <ion-header>
      <ion-toolbar>
        <ion-title>{{ isEditing() ? 'Editar Cliente' : 'Nuevo Cliente' }}</ion-title>
        <ion-button slot="end" fill="clear" (click)="didDismiss.emit()">Cerrar</ion-button>
      </ion-toolbar>
    </ion-header>
    <ion-content class="ion-padding">
      <form [formGroup]="clientForm" (ngSubmit)="onSubmit()">
        <ion-item lines="full" [class.ion-invalid]="clientForm.get('nombre')?.invalid && clientForm.get('nombre')?.touched" class="ion-touched">
          <ion-label position="stacked">Nombre Completo</ion-label>
          <ion-input formControlName="nombre" placeholder="Nombre completo" type="text" maxlength="40"></ion-input>
          @if (clientForm.get('nombre')?.invalid && clientForm.get('nombre')?.touched) {
            <ion-note slot="error">
              @if (clientForm.get('nombre')?.errors?.['required']) {
                El nombre es requerido.
              } @else if (clientForm.get('nombre')?.errors?.['minlength']) {
                Debe tener al menos 3 caracteres.
              } @else if (clientForm.get('nombre')?.errors?.['maxlength']) {
                No debe superar los 40 caracteres.
              } @else if (clientForm.get('nombre')?.errors?.['maxWords']) {
                No debe exceder de un nombre y apellido (2 palabras).
              } @else if (clientForm.get('nombre')?.errors?.['pattern']) {
                Solo se permiten letras y espacios.
              }
            </ion-note>
          }
        </ion-item>
        <ion-item lines="full" [class.ion-invalid]="clientForm.get('telefono')?.invalid && clientForm.get('telefono')?.touched" class="ion-touched">
          <ion-label position="stacked">Teléfono</ion-label>
          <ion-input formControlName="telefono" placeholder="Ej: +54 9..." type="tel" maxlength="15"></ion-input>
          @if (clientForm.get('telefono')?.invalid && clientForm.get('telefono')?.touched) {
            <ion-note slot="error">
              @if (clientForm.get('telefono')?.errors?.['required']) {
                El teléfono es requerido.
              } @else if (clientForm.get('telefono')?.errors?.['minlength']) {
                Debe tener al menos 8 caracteres.
              } @else if (clientForm.get('telefono')?.errors?.['maxlength']) {
                No debe superar los 15 caracteres.
              } @else if (clientForm.get('telefono')?.errors?.['pattern']) {
                Solo números, espacios, '+' y '-'.
              }
            </ion-note>
          }
        </ion-item>
        
        <ion-button expand="block" type="submit" [disabled]="clientForm.invalid || isSaving()" class="ion-margin-top">
          {{ isSaving() ? 'Guardando...' : (isEditing() ? 'Actualizar Cliente' : 'Guardar Cliente') }}
        </ion-button>
      </form>
    </ion-content>
  </ng-template>
</ion-modal>

components.name: PageComponent
components.template:
Pages in Storybook

We recommend building UIs with a component-driven process starting with atomic components and ending with pages.

Render pages with mock data. This makes it easy to build and review page states without needing to navigate to them in your app. Here are some handy patterns for managing page data in Storybook:

  • Use a higher-level connected component. Storybook helps you compose such data from the "args" of child component stories
  • Assemble data in the page component from your services. You can mock these services out using Storybook.

Get a guided tutorial on component-driven development at Storybook tutorials . Read more in the docs .

Tip Adjust the width of the canvas with the Viewports addon in the toolbar

import { Component } from '@angular/core'; import { CommonModule } from '@angular/common'; import { HeaderComponent } from './header.component'; import type { User } from './user'; @Component({ selector: 'storybook-page', standalone: true, imports: [CommonModule, HeaderComponent], template: `

Render pages with mock data. This makes it easy to build and review page states without needing to navigate to them in your app. Here are some handy patterns for managing page data in Storybook:

  • Use a higher-level connected component. Storybook helps you compose such data from the "args" of child component stories
  • Assemble data in the page component from your services. You can mock these services out using Storybook.

Get a guided tutorial on component-driven development at Storybook tutorials . Read more in the docs .

Tip Adjust the width of the canvas with the Viewports addon in the toolbar
`, styleUrls: ['./page.css'], }) export class PageComponent { user: User | null = null; doLogout() { this.user = null; } doLogin() { this.user = { name: 'Jane Doe' }; } doCreateAccount() { this.user = { name: 'Jane Doe' }; } }
